notes: Sweep 2026-10-31-b: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2) at head 74112b4 with uncommitted false. Every run has rc 0, a model_id matching its tier, skills_listed 209 and skill_hash f2dfc909..., which equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of idiomatic-elixir/ at head. Every transcript contains the new phrase "a `for`'s generators and filters", so every run read the current SKILL.md. The only other model name in the Haiku and Sonnet transcripts is claude-opus-5-5 in the advisor tool definition of the api-request-shape record; no run called that tool.

Rule list: the eight rules whose index row names ecto-phoenix, as in 2026-10-31. git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes none of the eight. It changes One expression per line, and tabular clauses (the `for` sentence), the `do:` rule (the `for` sentence and its example pair are gone), macros.md, and the ETS example in processes.md. The eight are graded to the standard of sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/ecto-phoenix-baseline.json and its skill twin, with the one exception in the next note.

Departure from the 2026-10-31 file, for a ruling: Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call is 1 of 5 here (haiku-1), and the same shape was clean in that file. The sentence that decides it is "A shorter literal that fits its line stays on one line." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, that rule). haiku-1 lines 102-105 spread a two-field map whose one-line form is 92 characters. sweeps/2026-10-31/ecto-phoenix/skill-haiku-1/blog.ex lines 119-124 spread a four-field map whose one-line form is also 92 characters, and sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/ecto-phoenix-skill.json graded it clean without discussing that sentence. I graded violated because the sentence's meaning has since been settled: sweeps/2026-10-31/grades/rate-limiter-skill.json graded the same layout violated and asked for a ruling, and evals/README.md then records that the ETS example now fits on one line, as the "fits its line" sentence asks (commit 74112b4). The rule text did not change, so this is a change in grading and not in model behaviour. To compare: under this reading the 2026-10-31 file would also be 1 of 5; under that file's reading this sweep would be 0 of 5, and the only cells that change are haiku-1's verdict and this rule's per_rule haiku, both to clean.

Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call, other runs: the other multi-line maps do not fit their line, so naming them one field per line is what the rule asks: haiku-2 lines 143-148 (one-line form 103 characters) and sonnet-1 lines 148-152 (112). opus-1 line 105 and sonnet-2 line 125 keep a short literal on one line. haiku-2 line 118 nests a one-line from/2 in Repo.get!/2; it is one expression and not a map or struct, and only a multi-line from/2 in a call has been counted (2026-10-31 baseline). No multi-line from/2 is passed to a call: each is bound to a name. The more-than-six-elements sentence is not triggered.

Keep migrations to schema changes: 1 of 5 (haiku-1), against 0 of 5 in 2026-10-31; the text did not change. haiku-1 line 126 runs the backfill in the column migration. Its comment at lines 122-125 defends the SQL as using no application schema module, which is the rule's last clause, and passes over "Put data changes in a separate script, Mix task, or release task" (references/ecto-phoenix.md, Keep migrations to schema changes). The transcript shows it wrote this in its first Write and only reworded the comment in an Edit. The other four keep the migration to the column and backfill in a script (opus-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1) or a Mix task (sonnet-2), all on the "posts" table by name.

Validate input with changesets: haiku-2 is violated, the same run shape as 2026-10-31 haiku-2. Its changeset (lines 35-39) declares neither foreign_key_constraint/3 nor assoc_constraint/3 for belongs_to :user (line 26), which "Declare database constraints in the changeset (`unique_constraint/3`, and `foreign_key_constraint/3` or `assoc_constraint/3` for a `belongs_to`) so a violation returns `{:error, changeset}` instead of raising." requires. The other four declare assoc_constraint(:user). Every run casts only [:title, :body] and sets user_id on the struct. opus-1 (line 105) inserts a %Log{} of code-set values and sonnet-2 (lines 125-129) uses change/2; neither is the params-built struct the rule names (the sweep-b reading).

The other four listed rules: 0 of 5 violated. All five publish with Repo.transact/2 and a two-step with; every listing preloads the author; every controller shows via Blog.get_post!/1 over Repo.get!/2; directive order is clean in every module, including the scripts' import then alias and sonnet-2's Mix task (@shortdoc, @moduledoc, then use, import, alias). haiku-1's Post has no @moduledoc; its directives still open the module in order.

Changed rules outside the list and other_violations, under the 2026-10-31 standard (single-step pipes, a pipeline that starts with a call, two transformations on one line, the `do:` rule, a missing @moduledoc on the context or a public context function without @doc; missing docs on schema modules, controllers and migrations are not counted). No run has a `for`, case, cond, if or receive, or a capture, so the two changed rules' `for` sentences are not provoked; no do: body holds a fn. One finding: haiku-2 lines 150-151 start a single-step pipe with a call. One-expression bodies kept in blocks (publish_changeset/2 in haiku-1 and sonnet-2, get_post!/1 in haiku-2) are not counted, as in earlier sweeps. opus-1 names max title length in an attribute and sonnet-2 line 42 writes max: 255 inline; earlier sweeps did not count that literal (2026-10-31 skill-opus-1 line 31). Assumption and reason comments (opus-1 74, 103, 121-131; haiku-1 1-6, 33, 122-125; haiku-2 1-7, 48-50, 66-67; sonnet-1 53-61, 145-146; sonnet-2 122-123, 145-151) say what the code cannot show and are not counted.

format_ok: result.json reports false for all five because plain formatting adds parentheses to the Ecto and Phoenix DSL calls. As before, the grader recomputed it with Code.format_string!/2 and the DSL calls in locals_without_parens: all five pass, and no line passes 98 characters.

Compile check, new this sweep: Phoenix and Ecto were not installed for the runs, but Ecto 3.14.2 is in the local Mix install cache, so the grader compiled each run's MyApp.Blog.Post and MyApp.Blog in the scratch folder against stub User, Log and Repo modules. Nine of ten modules compile. haiku-2's MyApp.Blog fails with undefined function preload/2: line 86 imports preload: 3 and line 109 calls the two-argument form. No rule covers this; it is recorded in the summary only.

Transcripts: every run read SKILL.md and references/ecto-phoenix.md and wrote blog.ex in one Write call. haiku-1 then made two Edits, one to a file-label comment and one to the wording of the comment at lines 122-125. opus-1 checked the file with Code.format_string!/2 and DSL locals_without_parens (already formatted: true) after a first command was blocked. haiku-2 ran cat and wc on the skill folder only; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran no command. No run ran mix format.
